topic: Automated EEG artifact handling and downstream decoding

framework.name: PICO
framework.rationale: The researcher applies a cleaning method (an intervention) and asks how its output compares with expert annotation and what it does to decoding - an effect question, so PICO; not PECO (nothing is an exposure) and not PCC (the question is not an inventory).

slots.value: scalp EEG recordings from human participants, any paradigm
slots.reason: nameable (authors write EEG) and it separates the topic from MEG / fMRI

slots.value: automated artifact rejection or removal pipelines
manual expert annotation or visual inspection
slots.reason: control arms are rarely named in titles; AND-ing them would drop most papers - applied at screening and reached by the contrast variant

slots.value: agreement with expert labels; decoding accuracy after cleaning
slots.reason: outcome metrics are often unstated in titles and abstracts; applied at screening

outcomes.text: agreement between automated and expert artifact labels
change in downstream decoding accuracy after cleaning

protocol.timeframe_reason: the reference pipelines (FASTER 2010, PREP 2015, Autoreject 2017) are still the baselines; the snowball recovers anything older
protocol.setting: CPU / Apple MPS, minutes-to-hours per experiment

inclusion.text: applies an automated artifact rejection or removal method to scalp EEG
reports agreement with expert or manual labels
or reports a downstream decoding or classification result before and after cleaning

exclusion.text: hardware or electrode design without any artifact-handling evaluation
